column1: # Every separate Go module (a go.mod) under ee/ and examples/ is run by a lane
# in .github/workflows/test.yml that DISCOVERS it (`find <root> -name go.mod`),
# unless a row here says otherwise. Read by the two discovering lanes (they
# skip the modules listed) and by
# tests/regression-test-required/nested_module_discovery_test.sh, which fails
# on a module that is in neither a discovering lane nor this file, on a row
# with no reason, and on a row whose module no longer exists.
# Three tab-separated columns: module, disposition, reason.
#   covered-by:<job-id>   the module is run by that job in test.yml by name (a
#                         `cd <module>` step followed by go test/vet); the guard
#                         verifies the step and reports whether the job's `if:`
#                         excludes pull_request
#   excluded              no job runs the module, for the reason given, which
#                         must name the issue where the debt is tracked (#NNNN)
# Boundary (master, 2026-09-08): the ROOT ee module (ee/go.mod) is W1-D's
# (#3699); its packages are selected by test.yml's enterprise arms and are not
# nested modules. It is listed here so the census is the whole set of go.mod
# files under ee/ and examples/, and so a second root module cannot appear
# unnoticed.
ee
column3: the root ee module; its packages are selected by the enterprise arms (unit-tests-enterprise on the PR tier, unit-tests-enterprise-realpg in the merge queue), which is #3699's subject and W1-D's PR, not a nested module

column1: ee/platform/aws-marketplace/license-validator
column3: TestGracePeriod fails on a clean checkout with day-boundary arithmetic against the wall clock (expected 6 got 7, expected 0 got 1); it has never run in CI; a lane that includes it would be red on every PR until the test is fixed; row on #3699

column1: ee/platform/aws-marketplace/marketplace-subscription-handler
column3: BUILDS since #3940; built by build-every-go-module and not unit-tested by any lane. The previous reason - sesv2 v1.32.7 is a revision that does not exist, so go.sum could never be generated - was correct and is retired here rather than deleted: the pin is now resolved, the dead `marketplacemetering` import that stopped the source compiling is GONE, and with it the require - `go mod tidy` dropped it, so this module now has NO marketplacemetering dependency at all. It is NOT 'aligned to v1.36.4': whoever implements #3980 must add the require back and pin `v1.36.4` to match `ee/go.mod` and `platform/go.mod`. `sesv2 v1.73.0` is what tidy resolved and is the only sesv2 pin in the tree, so no alignment claim applies to it either. Its AWS Marketplace metering ResolveCustomer call is still commented out; that gap is #3980, not this row. Row on #3940

column1: ee/platform/orchestrator/llm
column3: [no-build] ORPHANED BY #3252 and deliberately NOT fixed by #3940. Adding the require its go.mod is missing produces an AMBIGUOUS IMPORT, not a build: this go.mod declares axonflow/platform/orchestrator/llm, which shadows a real package inside the platform module. ee/go.mod replaces axonflow/ee/platform/orchestrator/llm, a path this directory does not declare, so the replace is inert and nothing can reach these 16 files; platform/orchestrator/Dockerfile records "EE orchestrator modules: none, all seven are built from platform/ (#3252)". Making it build would make dead code look alive. Wants a delete-or-revive decision, not a go.mod edit; row on #3940
